# Ai Observability Evaluation

Human-readable reference generated from the same rules as the NewHeap consumer skills.

## Contents

- [Keep AI telemetry content-free and gate changes with evaluations](#keep-ai-telemetry-content-free-and-gate-changes-with-evaluations)

## Keep AI telemetry content-free and gate changes with evaluations

Execute model calls through bounded profile and budget policy, separate usage from audit, and compare versioned Microsoft AI Evaluation datasets before changing production defaults.

## Preferred approach

Use `INhAiChatExecutor` when a model call needs NewHeap profile selection,
declared and remaining-run budgets, deadlines, content-free OpenTelemetry and
usage accounting. It returns standard Microsoft `ChatResponse` and
`ChatResponseUpdate` objects. Streaming resolution remains a structured result;
enumeration preserves cancellation and always records cleanup and time to first
token. After enumeration, await `NhAiChatStream.Completion`: successful end and
provider dependency failure are explicit `TaskResult` outcomes, while caller
cancellation remains cancellation.

A slow assistant turn explains itself: its log line and `NhAssistantConversationTurnResult.Timings`
(`NhAssistantTurnTimings`) give the total, preparation with its MCP, retrieval and file parts, model time
and calls, tool time and the time to the first text, as numbers without content (SPM-383). The model
part adds up the same `NhAiUsageRecord` durations a usage sink receives.

A governed deadline is an expected outcome, not an exception. When the profile's timeout or the
invocation context's `Deadline` passes before the model answers, after any retry the profile
allows, `GetResponseAsync` returns the failed result `NhAiModelFailureCodes.Timeout`
(`ai-model-timeout`); a stream ends its enumeration without an exception, keeps the updates it
already delivered, and completes with that failed result. A cancellation the caller did not
request, such as the provider HTTP client's own timeout, counts the same. The usage record and the
`ai.model.invoke` activity carry outcome `NhAiOutcomeKind.TimedOut` and finish reason
`timed-out` (`NhAiModelFinishReasons`). Only the caller's own token still throws
`OperationCanceledException`, recorded as `TerminalFailure` with finish reason `cancelled`. In
both cases the call keeps its one budget reservation and writes one usage record with the same
`ModelCallId`, so a budget manager settles it as any other call. Propagate the failed result like
the other `NhAiModelFailureCodes`; the Agent Framework adapter throws it as
`NhAiAgentModelCallException` with the code, and the assistant ends such a turn with
`assistant-turn-timeout` (`assistant-consult-timeout` in a consultation).

A call that fails at the provider, after any retry the profile allows, returns the failed result
`NhAiModelFailureCodes.DependencyUnavailable` (`ai-model-dependency-unavailable`) for every cause,
so existing mappings keep working, and says why without content. `NhAiModelProviderFailure.Of(result)`
on the executor's result, or on a failed `NhAiChatStream.Completion`, gives the HTTP status, the
provider's error code (at most 64 safe characters), the type of the exception and an
`NhAiModelProviderFailureKind`: `Transient` for 408, 429, 5xx, timeouts and broken connections,
`Authentication` for 401 and 403, `Request` for another 4xx and `Unknown` otherwise. The usage record
carries the same value as `NhAiUsageRecord.ProviderFailure`, the `ai.model.invoke` activity tags
`http.response.status_code`, `newheap.ai.provider.code` and `newheap.ai.provider.failure_kind`, and the
executor logs one warning with them, never the provider's message, which can repeat part of a key or
the request. A copied `TaskResult` keeps only the code and message, so read the failure from the
executor's own result. The executor reads `HttpRequestException` itself (its status, or its
`HttpRequestError` such as `ConnectionError` when it got no answer). Provider SDKs that throw their own
exception type need an `INhAiModelProviderFailureReader`, registered with
`AddModelProviderFailureReader<TReader>()`, that returns `NhAiModelProviderError` with the status and
code it reads, and `null` for other exceptions; NewHeap references no provider SDK. The sample's
`SampleOpenAiFailureReader` reads the status of the OpenAI client's `ClientResultException` and only the
`error.code` field of its answer (SPM-232). A status a reader returns also decides the retry of a
retry-eligible profile. Treat `Authentication` and `Request` as configuration or request errors to
fix, not as an outage.

Keep operational telemetry, application audit and usage accounting in separate
sinks. Usage records may include stable versions and hashes, bounded scope
identifiers, token counts, character counts, duration, finish reason and a model
identifier hash. Count and correlate model calls by `NhAiUsageRecord.ModelCallId`:
every governed model call gets its own id, which its retries, its budget
reservation (`NhAiBudgetRequest.ModelCallId`), its `ai.model.invoke` activity
(`newheap.ai.model_call_id`) and its usage record share. `InvocationId` names the
invocation context, which several calls of one turn share. They must not include prompts, responses, tool arguments,
retrieved documents, credentials or provider error bodies. Applications map the
retention categories to their own duration, residency, legal-hold and deletion
policies.

Use the packable AI Test fixtures with `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation` for
versioned datasets and content-free reports. Treat missing or inconclusive metric
interpretations as failed. Deterministic evaluators belong in normal CI. Live
judge/model evaluations are explicit, credentialed, budgeted and reproducible;
compare and accept the baseline before changing a recommended model, prompt,
tool catalog or agent asset.

Structured output is checked where the provider checks it. NewHeap passes a
`ChatOptions.ResponseFormat` schema on unchanged; normalizing it for a provider stays with the
application. Providers in strict mode refuse a schema whose `$ref` names anything but the root
(`#`) or an entry of the root's `$defs` (`#/$defs/name`), whose objects do not set
`additionalProperties` to `false`, or whose objects leave a property out of `required`. Set
`StrictStructuredOutput` on `NhAiDeterministicChatClient` or `NhAiScriptedChatClient` to refuse
such a request in tests as the provider would, with an `HttpRequestException` of status 400 that the
executor reports as `ai-model-dependency-unavailable` without a retry, or call
`NhAiStrictStructuredOutput.Validate` on the schema for every `NhAiStrictSchemaViolation` with its
JSON pointer. What Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.9 generates with `AIJsonUtilities.CreateJsonSchema`:

- Without `AIJsonSchemaTransformOptions { DisallowAdditionalProperties = true, RequireAllProperties = true }`,
  and so with `ChatResponseFormat.ForJsonSchema<T>()` as it is, every object stays open and a
  parameter with a default value, such as `int Limit = 10`, is not required: refused. Generate with
  those transform options.
- A repeated object type, such as `Order(Address Billing, Address Shipping)`, is written out at each
  property: accepted.
- A nullable object, such as `Contact(string Name, Address? Work)`, is required with
  `"type": ["object", "null"]`: accepted.
- A list element type used twice, such as `Board(IReadOnlyList<Line> Open, IReadOnlyList<Line> Done)`,
  refers to the second use as `"items": { "$ref": "#/properties/open/items" }`: refused. Move `Line`
  into `$defs` and refer to `#/$defs/line` from both lists.
- A type that contains itself at the root, such as `Node(string Name, IReadOnlyList<Node> Children)`,
  refers to `#`: accepted.
- A recursive type below the root, such as `Tree(string Title, Branch Root)` with
  `Branch(string Label, IReadOnlyList<Branch> Branches)`, refers to
  `#/properties/root/properties/branches`: refused. Move `Branch` into `$defs`.

SPM-335 shows an application's own normalization: `ProjectAiStructuredOutput` generates the schema
with closed objects and every property required, moves each JSON-pointer reference target into
`$defs`, and the status digest's tests prove the result with the strict deterministic client.

Score prompt injection through documents on a recorded turn rather than on hand-written prompts:
run the assistant turn with the malicious document, record the model request, and evaluate it with
what the turn did as `EvaluationContext`. The case passes only when the document's text reaches the
model behind the external-file marker as untrusted retrieved data (`newheap.trust`
`untrusted-retrieved`) and never in the instructions, the turn offers the same tools as without the
document, and a change the model then asks for waits for approval without running (SPM-233).

## Avoid

- Logging or tagging message text, model output, retrieved content or provider exception bodies.
- Combining business audit history and usage allocation into one universal platform database.
- Counting model calls by distinct `InvocationId`; one invocation context serves several calls, so
  count `ModelCallId`.
- Treating an inconclusive evaluation as a pass.
- Recommending a model upgrade based only on compilation or a single live demonstration.
- Keeping a streaming provider call alive after the consumer cancels enumeration.
- Catching `OperationCanceledException` to detect a model timeout; read `ai-model-timeout` from the result.
- Logging a provider exception or its message to diagnose a failed model call; log
  `NhAiModelProviderFailure`, and register an `INhAiModelProviderFailureReader` for an SDK whose
  exception the executor does not know.
- Reading a provider's error message or whole response body in a reader; read the status and the code
  field only.
- Expecting NewHeap to normalize a structured-output schema, or testing structured output only with a
  client that accepts every schema.

## Verification

Capture activities, metrics, usage and reports and serialize them in tests.
Assert that protected fixture strings are absent while profile versions, hashes,
tokens, latency, time to first token, finish and cancellation outcomes remain.
Assert that two calls in one invocation context get two `ModelCallId`s while a
retried call keeps one, shared with its budget reservation.
Also force a provider exception during stream enumeration and assert that the
stream ends with a safe failed completion rather than leaking provider details.
Let a provider refuse a call with 401, 400 and 503 and without an answer, through the executor and
through a registered reader for an SDK exception, and assert the status, code and kind on the result,
the usage record and the warning log, that the provider's message appears in none of them, and that
only a transient status is retried.
Let a model wait past a short profile timeout and past the invocation deadline, for a call and a
stream, and assert `ai-model-timeout`, outcome `TimedOut`, finish reason `timed-out` and one
reservation and usage record with the same `ModelCallId`; cancel the caller's token and assert
that cancellation still throws. Send each structured-output schema to a client with
`StrictStructuredOutput`.
Run the deterministic dataset on every relevant change, and run controlled live
evaluation only in its opt-in pipeline. SPM-232, SPM-233 and SPM-335 are the executable
references.
